name: rust-brotli (Dropbox Rust port of Brotli)
workload: Dropbox 2016 post: decompression of 4 MB Brotli blocks by the safe-Rust decompressor (now the separate rust-brotli-decompressor crate that rust-brotli depends on) against the vanilla C decompressor built with gcc-4.9 -O3; no compression-speed table exists in the repo or the post snippets.
claimed_speedup: Not faster than C. Dropbox post (snippet only): safe Rust decompressor ran at 72% of the speed of the vanilla -O3 C decompressor, 217 MB/s on an Intel Core i7-4790 @ 3.60GHz; skipping allocator zeroing raised it to 224 MB/s (+3.2%, derived from page data). Author's 2017 Hacker News comment (snippet only): 80-90% of the original's speed on average, with some files compressing faster in Rust than with the original codec. The book's 'over 10 percent after removing initialization and bounds checking' compares the port with its own earlier version, not with C.
compiler_and_flags: C baseline: gcc-4.9 -O3 (per post snippet). Rust compiler, version and flags for the 2016 measurement not stated. Current Cargo.toml release profile sets lto = true, incremental = false.
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4790 CPU @ 3.60GHz (per post snippet, 2016)
tradeoffs: Memory-safe (library description says all included code is safe), no_std capable with a pluggable allocator, SECCOMP-friendly front-loaded allocation, multithreaded compression, catable streams, C-compatible FFI, custom dictionaries. Encoder is stated to be bitwise identical to the C compressor at quality 0-9; quality 10 and 11 differ (default 9.5). Cost is decoder speed: the decompressor README lists an extra indirection in the hgroups, array bounds checks on every access and no aligned 64/128-bit loads from [u8] as expected losses.
caveats: Does not beat the baseline on any number found: every figure puts Rust at or below C. The 72% / 217 MB/s / 224 MB/s figures come from search-result snippets of the Dropbox post (2016, i7-4790); dropbox.tech could not be opened in this session (DNS failure), so they are snippet only and unverified; one search summary also mentioned 249 MB/s and 82% of C, not confirmed by a second snippet. The post measured decompression, whose code lives in dropbox/rust-brotli-decompressor, not in this repo. The Hacker News comment (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=14903412) is a 2017 self-report seen only as a snippet; it gives no per-file numbers, CPU or flags. The repo README and the decompressor README carry no benchmark numbers. Independent reports show Rust slower than C: github.com/dropbox/rust-brotli/issues/76 (comment, 2023) decompressing a 50 GB texture tarball took 160 s against 90 s for Google's tool (hardware, flags and quality not stated); github.com/Vaibhav91one/android-doctor/issues/74 measured brotli crate 9.0 decode at 250 MB/s against 391 MB/s for the C reference via Python brotli on a 10-core Apple Silicon (release build, no flags), later 4.65 s against 2.28 s (2.04x) on firmware images. No public benchmark code with compiler, flags and CPU exists, so tier A and B do not apply. Kept as a flagged entry: the library is notable and maintained, but it is a safety-first port that is slower than C.
